chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) saw a sheikh who had never performed Hajj and was unable to perform Hajj due to his old age, so he ordered him to equip a man to perform Hajj on his behalf.

key_terms.عَنْهُ: on his behalf / in substitution for him
key_terms.يُجَهِّزَ: to equip / to prepare / to fund

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly person who cannot physically perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *Hajj al-Badal* (substitutionary pilgrimage) for those incapacitated by old age, emphasizing that the physical burden of preparation and travel is borne by the proxy. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the obligation remains on the individual, but the performance is delegated, distinguishing it from the general obligation of Hajj al-Fard. The hadith underscores the accessibility of divine commandments, ensuring that the elderly are not excluded from this pillar due to physical limitations.
